name: Smoky Mountains
tagline: Where the Mountains Do the Talking
description: The Smoky Mountains corridor—anchored by Gatlinburg, Pigeon Forge, and Knoxville—is America's most visited national park gateway fused with Dolly Parton's entertainment empire and an increasingly cool college-town food scene. Twelve million people a year come for the mountains and stay for the moonshine, pancake houses, and roller coasters.

identity.vibe: Family-vacation Appalachia meets honky-tonk mountain town — think Disney energy wrapped in moonshine jars and fall foliage.

nexus_grid.title: Theme Parks & Attractions
nexus_grid.description: Dollywood, dinner shows, and the Gatlinburg attraction strip are the trip anchor for 70%+ of visitors.

nexus_grid.title: Great Smoky Mountains National Park
nexus_grid.description: Free entry, 850+ miles of trails, waterfalls, wildlife, and Cades Cove — the outdoor backbone of every trip.

nexus_grid.title: Moonshine & Distillery Trail
nexus_grid.description: Free tastings, live music, and 100-year-old recipes — the moonshine trail is the adult version of the attraction strip.

nexus_grid.title: Cabin Rentals
nexus_grid.description: Hot tubs, mountain views, game rooms — the cabin IS the vacation for many visitors.

modes.label: Family Fun
modes.description: Theme parks, dinner shows, aquariums, easy hikes, and pancake houses — the Smokies were built for families.

modes.label: Mountain Adventure
modes.description: 850+ miles of trails, waterfalls, and wildlife in America's most visited national park.

modes.label: Foodie Trail
modes.description: From James Beard-winning Knoxville kitchens to heritage pancake houses and creekside steakhouses.

modes.label: Moonshine & Spirits
modes.description: Distilleries, wine trails, craft breweries, and 100-year-old recipes across three towns.

modes.label: Couples Escape
modes.description: Cabin hot tubs, speakeasy cocktails, mountaintop sunsets, and fondue date nights.

modes.label: After Dark
modes.description: Rooftop bars, live music stages, speakeasies, and the Parkway lit up after dark.

modes.label: Arts & Heritage
modes.description: Appalachian artisan communities, historic theaters, bluegrass music, and mountain craftsmanship.

modes.label: Just Vibin'
modes.description: Slow mornings, scenic drives, wine tastings, foot soaks, and cabin time.

transit.local_transport: You need a car. Period. The Parkway (US-441) is the main artery connecting Sevierville → Pigeon Forge → Gatlinburg, and it gets brutally congested in peak season. Gatlinburg has a free trolley system that covers the downtown strip and some outlying areas. Pigeon Forge has a trolley too ($1 per ride). Uber/Lyft exist but supply is thin outside Knoxville. Knoxville itself is reasonably walkable downtown (Market Square / Old City / Gay Street corridor).

_legacy_transit.label: Drive
_legacy_transit.text: Nashville to Gatlinburg: 225 miles via I-40 E, ~3.5 hours. Atlanta to Gatlinburg: 200 miles via I-75 N, ~3.5 hours. Charlotte to Gatlinburg: 260 miles via I-40 W, ~4 hours.

_legacy_transit.label: Fly
_legacy_transit.text: McGhee Tyson Airport (TYS) in Knoxville — 45 min to Pigeon Forge, 1 hr to Gatlinburg. Allegiant, American, Delta, United, Frontier all fly in. No direct rail.

side_trips.name: Townsend - The Quiet Side of the Smokies
side_trips.distance: 35 min from Gatlinburg / 45 min from Knoxville
side_trips.pitch: The anti-Gatlinburg. No strip, no neon, just a sleepy mountain town at the western park entrance with great access to Cades Cove and uncrowded trails.

side_trips.name: Sevierville
side_trips.pitch: Dolly Parton's actual hometown. More local, less tourist. Better outlet shopping, great distilleries, and the best statue of Dolly you'll find.

side_trips.name: Cherokee, North Carolina
side_trips.distance: 1 hr from Gatlinburg via Newfound Gap Rd
side_trips.pitch: Cross over the Smokies into North Carolina. Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians homeland. Casino, cultural museum, and Oconaluftee Visitor Center.

side_trips.name: Asheville, North Carolina
side_trips.pitch: Craft beer capital of the South, Blue Ridge Parkway, and Biltmore Estate. A perfect overnight extension for foodies and culture seekers.

concierge.name: The Ridge Runner
concierge.greeting: Well hey there — welcome to the Smokies. I've been runnin' these ridges for thirty-some years and I've got opinions on everything from pancakes to park trails. What can I help you find?

_legacy.hero_sub: Waterfalls, Dollywood's extended hours, tubing the Little River, and nightly fireworks over Pigeon Forge. Summer is full throttle.
